title: The signed JWT assertion sent as jwt_token, derived from the private key
summary: A synthetic three-segment signed assertion as the jwt_token parameter of a raw form-encoded exchange request and of a curl form argument.
rationale: The assertion is derived from the private key, signed with RS256 and exchanged for an access token, and it is the only place the key's work leaves the developer's machine: the exchange request carries client_id, client_secret and jwt_token and no parameter for the key itself. Adobe recommends that it live a few minutes, but the pages state no maximum lifetime Adobe enforces, so a captured assertion is not recorded as expired or harmless, and no page says it is a credential of the key's family either. The assertion is therefore neither the private key nor shown to be a non-secret; its handling, and that of the client_secret beside it (a separate credential), are left to their own records. The fixture value is three base64url segments of obviously fake content: a header naming RS256, a payload of synthetic claims and a signature segment that encodes the words SYNTHETIC-signature-never-issued, so it cannot verify against any key.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted: the assertion is derived and short-lived by recommendation, Adobe states no enforced maximum lifetime, and no source states whether a captured assertion is sensitive or part of this family. An Adobe statement of the enforced lifetime or of the assertion's confidentiality would settle it (open question derived-assertion-and-secret-companions).

sources.supports: The exchange request has three URL-encoded body parameters, client_id, client_secret and jwt_token (a base-64 encoded JSON Web Token signed with a private key); the table lists no parameter that carries the private key itself.
sources.locator: sections "Exchanging JWT to retrieve an access token" and "Request parameters"

sources.supports: The JWT must be signed with the private key of a digital signing certificate associated with the integration's API key, using RS256; the private key generates the signature and the Adobe Developer Console receives a public key to validate it.
An exp claim is required and a very short-lived JWT (a few minutes) is recommended; longer-lived JWTs that are reused are discouraged.
sources.locator: section "Required Claims for a Service Account JWT", exp claim

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. No outcome is asserted: the open question named in the expectation is what would have to be settled first.
